transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this. 

I came in because... well, I guess I've started doing some things at work—I do bookkeeping—and at school that just don't make a lot of sense lately. It's probably nothing too serious, really, just some silly habits, you know? Like, instead of filing, I'll start lining receipts all the way across the floor. Or I'll catch myself tapping the calculator in sets of nine. Just little quirks... is that the right kind of thing to tell you? 

I'm a little embarrassed to admit it, but sometimes I'll also just get stuck standing by the copier with my hands held up in the air, and I won't put them down until someone asks if I'm okay. I know it sounds really strange, and I don't want you to think badly of me... I just don't want to cause any trouble at my job. Does that make sense? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel like you have to line those receipts up in a specific way or count those taps on the calculator to a specific number because it would feel wrong if you didn't?

Um, actually... no, not really. I hope it's okay to say that. It's not like I get a bad feeling or feel like something terrible will happen if I don't do it. It doesn't really feel wrong to stop. I just... I kind of just find myself doing it, like I'm zoning out, I guess. 

I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for, or if it's not very helpful. I just want to make sure I'm being completely accurate for you so I don't waste your time. Does that still make sense?
Do you feel anxious or uneasy when you're not doing these things, like lining up the receipts or tapping the calculator?

Um, no, I don't think so. I really hope that's alright to say. I don't feel anxious or... or uneasy at all if I'm not doing them. 

It's honestly not a big deal, and I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. It's just sort of... neutral? Like I said, I just kind of zone out, but I definitely don't get nervous or upset if I stop or if I don't do it. 

Is that a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers so I can be as helpful as possible for you.
Do you feel like doing these things, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator, helps you feel more relaxed or comfortable in any way?

Um... no, not really. I hope it's okay that I keep saying no to these. It doesn't really make me feel relaxed, or... or more comfortable. It's honestly just something I catch myself doing. 

Like I said, it's really not a huge issue, and I definitely don't want you to think I'm doing it because I'm stressed or can't handle my job or anything like that. I'm actually doing fine there, I promise. It's just... I just kind of do it without thinking about it at all. 

Am I making sense? I really want to make sure I'm explaining this the right way so I'm not making your job harder.
Do you find yourself preferring things to be symmetrical or perfectly arranged in your daily life?

Um, no, not especially. I mean, I like things to look nice, sure, but I don't need them to be perfectly symmetrical or anything like that. I really hope I'm not coming across as, I don't know, too particular or difficult. 

I just kind of tidy up like anyone else would. It's not something I obsess over, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm sitting around all day making sure everything is perfectly straight. It's just... normal neatness, I guess? 

Does that sound alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Do you feel like you're in control when you're doing these things, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator?

Um, yeah, I definitely feel in control. I hope it's okay to say that, but I'm completely in control of it. 

I can stop whenever I want, really. It's not like I'm... compelled to do it or anything scary like that. I don't want you to worry that I'm losing control or that it's taking over my work, because it's definitely not. I just... I just happen to do it sometimes when it's quiet. 

I'm doing okay, right? I just want to make sure I'm not sounding like I'm completely falling apart or anything, because I really am managing fine.
Do you think there's a reason why you're doing these specific actions, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator, or do you think it's just a habit you've developed?

Um... I guess it's just a habit? Or maybe just me being a little quirky, I don't know. I really hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it needs to be. 

But I guess... well, I guess the reason I actually came in today is because I've started doing some of these things at work and, um, at school, and they... they don't really make a lot of sense. Like, the receipts thing, I was kind of... lining them up all the way across the floor. And the calculator, I tap it in sets of nine. 

And, um, sometimes I'll just go stand by the copier and hold my hands up in the air until someone walks by and asks if I'm okay. 

I know that sounds a little weird, and I'm really sorry if that makes me sound completely crazy. I promise I'm not trying to be disruptive or anything like that. It's just... it's just happening, and I thought maybe I should mention it. Is that okay? Did I explain that right?
Do you think your actions, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator, are related to trying to do things perfectly?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think so? I really hope I'm not giving the wrong impression here. I'm not trying to be a perfectionist or anything like that. 

The receipts and the calculator... it's not about making things perfect. It doesn't even have to look a certain way, honestly. It's just... I don't know, just something I do. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or obsessive about my work. I just want to do a good job, you know? 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you think something bad would happen if you didn't do these things, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator?

Um, no, no, definitely not. I don't think anything bad would happen at all. I hope that's the right answer, but I really don't feel like, you know, some disaster is going to strike if I don't tap the calculator. 

It's not like a superstition or anything scary like that. I'd hate for you to think I was, um, losing touch with reality or being superstitious. It's really just... just a thing I do sometimes. If I couldn't do it, I'd just... keep working. It wouldn't be a big deal at all. 

I'm making sense, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not making it sound worse than it is.
Do you feel like you're doing these things, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator, without really thinking about them beforehand?

Um, yeah, I guess so? I mean, I don't really plan them out or anything. It's not like I wake up and think, 'Today I'm going to line up all these receipts.' It just sort of... happens? 

Like I was saying before, that's kind of why I came in. I just find myself doing these things that don't really make a lot of sense, like the receipts across the floor, or the calculator thing, or... or just standing by the copier with my hands up. I don't really think about it before I do it, it just kind of starts. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound completely out of control. I'm still getting my work done, I promise! It's just... a little weird, I guess. Does that answer your question? I want to make sure I'm explaining it the way you need me to.
Do you feel like you're in a different state of mind when you're doing these things, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator?

Um, no, not really? I don't think I feel different, like, in my head or anything. I'm just... me, doing my job. 

I mean, I know it probably sounds a little strange when I talk about it, but when it's happening, I just feel like I'm working. I'm not in a trance or, um, checked out or anything like that. I'm still paying attention to everything around me. I really hope it doesn't seem like I'm, you know, zoning out on company time or something. I'm still totally focused. 

Is that what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound like I'm losing my grip or something, because I'm definitely not.
Do you remember everything that happens while you're doing these things, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator?

Oh, yeah, absolutely. I remember all of it. Um, it's not like I black out or lose time or anything scary like that. I know exactly what I'm doing the whole time. Like I said, I'm just working, looking at the numbers. My memory is actually really good, which you kind of need for bookkeeping, you know? 

I hope that's a good sign? That I remember it all, I mean. I definitely wouldn't want you to think I was having amnesia or forgetting how to do my job. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture here. I'm doing okay, right?
Do you think you could stop doing these things if you really wanted to?

Um, stop doing them? I... I think so? I mean, I haven't really tried to just force myself to stop, because, well, like I said, I didn't really realize it was a problem until people started looking at me funny. 

But I'm sure if I really concentrated, I could just... not do it. I mean, it's just silly stuff, right? Like the receipts on the floor, or the tapping the calculator nine times, or... or standing by the copier with my hands up. I only stop that one when someone walks by and asks if I'm okay. Which is, you know, kind of embarrassing, but it's not like I'm doing it on purpose to cause trouble or anything. 

I came in because I know it doesn't really make sense, and I want to fix it. I definitely don't want to be a disruption at work or at school. I'm trying really hard to be a good employee and student. Do you think it's something I can just learn to stop doing? I really want to do whatever you think is best.
Do you think doing these things helps you feel more in control of your environment or daily tasks?

Um, I don't know if it makes me feel in control exactly. I mean, maybe a little? But honestly, I think it just... it doesn't really make a lot of sense, even to me. 

That's actually kind of the whole reason I came in to see you. I just started doing these things at my bookkeeping job, and even at school, and I know they're, well, not normal. Like the receipts on the floor, or the tapping the calculator nine times... or even the thing by the copier where I just stand there with my hands up until someone asks if I'm alright. 

I know it sounds weird when I say it all out loud. I'm really not trying to be difficult or weird, I promise. I just want to figure out why I'm doing these things that don't make sense so I can stop. I want to be doing a good job and fitting in. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you ever feel like you're not fully aware of your surroundings when you're doing these things, like you're somewhere else in your mind?

No, no, I'm definitely fully aware. I'm right there in the room, I promise. It's not like I'm... like I'm spacing out or hallucinating or anything bad like that. I know exactly where I am and what's going on around me. 

I really try to stay focused, especially at work. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was, you know, out of it or not paying attention. I'm just doing my work, and then these... these little habits just kind of happen. But my mind is definitely present. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure you know I'm not losing touch with reality or anything. I'm still me, just... doing some silly things I need to fix.
Do you think your actions are related to trying to make things look a certain way or follow a specific pattern?

Um... a pattern? Well... yeah, I guess so. I'm a little embarrassed to admit this, because I really don't want you to think I'm weird or anything. But... sometimes at work, I get, well, convinced that certain invoice totals, or account numbers, and even the due dates are... like, messages about me. Like a pattern I'm supposed to figure out. 

I know it sounds really strange when I say it out loud. My supervisor actually sat down and showed me that they are just normal accounting entries, and I totally agreed with him because I want to be a good employee and not cause any problems. But... even after he showed me, deep down, I still kind of feel like they are tracking whether I understand the pattern. 

I'm trying really hard not to think that way, though. Does that make sense? I hope you don't think I'm crazy for saying that. I just want to be completely honest with you so I can fix it and do a better job.
Do you think there's a hidden meaning or code in the things you're doing, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator?

Oh, um... a hidden meaning in the tapping and the receipts? No, no, I don't think so. I really don't think there's a code in what *I'm* doing. It's just... I know it looks silly, but it's just me doing these weird little habits. 

I'm definitely not trying to send secret messages or anything like that, I promise. I just... I don't know why I do the tapping or the receipts. It's just a bad habit I've picked up, and I really want to stop doing it so I can just be a normal, good employee. I'm not trying to make things complicated, you know? I hope that's an okay answer. I just don't want you to think I'm doing it on purpose to be disruptive or anything.
Do you think there's a specific thought or belief that makes you want to do these things?

Um... a specific thought? I mean... not really? I don't think so. I really don't want to sound like I'm, you know, obsessing over things or having weird thoughts that make me act this way. 

I just... I think it's just stress from the job, maybe? Like, I want to make sure I'm doing everything perfectly so my supervisor is happy with my work. So maybe the thought is just... "do a good job"? 

I really don't think there's any strange belief behind it, I promise. I know I mentioned the thing about the invoice numbers earlier, and I'm still trying really hard to ignore that feeling, but the tapping and the receipts... that just feels like a nervous habit. I'm just trying to be a good bookkeeper. Is that... does that sound like a normal reason to you? I really hope I'm not making this sound worse than it is.
Do you think that the patterns or habits you're experiencing are related to any thoughts or beliefs that you hold to be true, even if they might seem unusual or unexplainable to others?

Um... I guess... yeah, it kind of goes back to what I mentioned a little bit ago. I'm really sorry to bring it up again, because I know how strange it sounds, and I really don't want you to think I'm... you know, completely out of touch with reality or anything. 

But... yeah, it's that feeling about the invoice totals and the account numbers and due dates. I just get so convinced that they are actual messages about me. And even when my supervisor takes the time to show me that they are just normal accounting entries—and I always agree with him, because I really do want to be a good employee and do things right—I still can't entirely shake it. Deep down, I still feel like they are tracking whether I understand the pattern. 

I know it's a really unusual thing to believe, and I'm trying so hard to push those thoughts away so I don't cause any problems at work. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right... I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need so I can get better.
Do you think the patterns or habits you're experiencing are related to a belief that something is true, even if others might not agree?

Um, yeah... I guess it is like that. I know I keep repeating myself, and I'm really sorry if I'm sounding like a broken record or being difficult. I really don't mean to be. 

It's just... like I said, it's those invoice totals and the account numbers and the due dates. I just... I get this feeling, and I get so convinced that they're actually messages specifically about me. And my supervisor is so nice about it, he really is, he sits down and shows me how they're just completely normal accounting entries. And I always tell him he's right, because I know he is, and I want to do a good job for him. 

But... even after he shows me, I still have this lingering feeling. I still feel like... like they're tracking whether I understand the pattern. I know it's probably just my mind playing tricks on me because I'm stressed about being a good bookkeeper, right? That happens to people sometimes? I really am trying to just focus on the work and ignore it. I hope it's okay that I still feel that way sometimes, even when I know better. I really am trying my best to just be normal about it.
